title: Make already-authorized Case Timeline filters operable from the actual same-origin HTML browser
goal: Complete the CAP-INV-110 read/filter user journey: the previously delivered source-authorized Case HTML page had only a table and page links. Reuse its existing GET /case-timeline typed-owner authorization and RFC3339/time/kind/query parser to let an analyst submit and reset filters directly via an accessible, no-JavaScript GET form, without creating any new data read or permission.
invariants: No new endpoint, data source, Search permission, cross-tenant read, handler or production IAM; reuses same existing independently owner-authorized GET Case Timeline.
The form sends only already validated Case selector and presentation-only kind, query, from, to and page-size; never principal/tenant/environment, session token or authorization flags.
Empty browser controls are omitted only during HTML GET presentation selection; unchanged strict JSON clients continue rejecting empty filter values.
No partial rendered source rows on malformed selectors, unauthorized Case or provider failure. All request-supplied text goes through html/template escaping and URL encoding.
Pagination links preserve validated active filters and reauthorize each new page. A fresh form submit resets offset to the first page.
CSP stays default-src none / no scripts, permitting only same-origin GET form-action self; all output no-store.
security_properties: HTML-only empty-field normalization is explicitly allowlisted to kind,q,from,to and does not accept duplicate/unknown keys.
Kind remains one of five allowed Timeline types and timestamps remain RFC3339Nano with from < to, page limit max200.
Search exclusively inspects existing source-authorized projected fields and cannot promote Command Incident.read to Investigate Case.read.

migration.rationale: Only an additional HTML GET form and HTML-only optional empty-filter semantics; no new storage, route or JSON API schema.

rollback.strategy: Remove HTML form and restore form-action none, retaining original HTML read and JSON API.
verification: Prior HTML and JSON test suites pass

inputs: CAP-INV-110 canonical §3,§11,§12 filter/read/temporal presentation; original cross-product Command selected Incident -> Case HTML route from PR #200
Parent immutable PR #200 SHA 12f92a24ee0d0be0b4bd298f7baef577f5fcdbaa under Git parent #199, distinct from canonical parent.
outputs: An analyst can interactively submit Case Timeline type/authorized metadata search/RFC3339 range and 1..200 page size through HTML without JavaScript.
Exact authorized query echoed into escaped form fields; Reset link removes filters; paging carries only validated view selectors.
JSON original strict parser and existing Command owner handoff unchanged.
acceptance_tests: Source-authorized Case HTML GET form accepts optional empty controls and renders only matching entries; preserves superseded/uncertain state.
One form submit resets offset, generates safe page continuation with active filters, and reset removes filters without token leakage.
Malformed/duplicate kinds/queries/range/page-size fail closed with no partial HTML; JSON API still rejects empty query/kind.
Hostile string filter is escaped; anonymous, foreign and insufficiently privileged Case cannot read the form or Timeline data.
Go race/vet and Timeline and cross-product Command HTTP plus engineering-kernel must pass on exact commit SHA.
definition_of_ready: Source existing J HTML Case read implemented with exact-SHA green workflows and no real IAM claimed
Existing strict server read selector and classified owner projection available; no new product decision or mutation
definition_of_done: Working local real HTTP form / case owner tests on exact new SHA, mandatory CI success
No serious regressions in strict JSON API or independent authorizations
Scoped independent L2 only if source/HTML security boundary changed materially; native GitHub approval/merge remain separate

performance_budget.rationale: Reuses bounded max5000 authorized entries and existing page size <=200, no new owner calls or additional parsing beyond <=7 GET parameters and HTML escaping.
